title: Audible
summary: Shadowfetch Linux 2.1.0 «Umbra» — a Debian-testing derivative with KDE Plasma 6. This release ships Intel Sound Open Firmware and the matching ALSA use-case profiles, so laptops whose audio DSP previously loaded no firmware and played nothing now have working sound out of the box. It also adds shadowfetch-facts, a read-only hardware inventory that records the source of every reading, and gives all sixteen helper commands a --help that is safe to run.

limitations.summary: The ISO cannot be copied onto a FAT32-formatted USB stick.
limitations.detail: FAT32 caps a single file at 4 GiB (4,294,967,295 bytes). This ISO is 4,509,110,272 bytes — 214,142,977 bytes (204 MiB) over that limit — so a plain file copy to a FAT32 stick fails with "file too large". Write the ISO to the USB device with an image writer (balenaEtcher, KDE ISO Image Writer, GNOME Disks) or dd instead of copying it onto a mounted FAT32 filesystem.
